newsitem.title: UK: Med oil products slip except steady, to firm fuel.
newsitem.headline: Med oil products slip except steady, to firm fuel.

text.p: Mediterranean oil products were easier apart from fuel oil on Tuesday, traders said.

Gasoline slipped $2-3 a tonne to about $218 and marking time awaiting consolidation of recent losses on U.S. gasoline and crude futures. The sector was looking fairly balanced with some demand in the east Med likely to be met by east Med supplies.
Naphtha also eased $2 or so to around $227 cif Med. Activity was muted with some petchem buyers looking to move their requirements into February to take advantage of weaker numbers.
Gas oil slipped around $4 a tonne on easier futures and volume was thin.

Traders said business was slow because vessels were difficult to obtain at economic rates and discussion was dominated by high demand for transport. Traders said operators wanted W250 for a 30,000 tonne gas oil vessel from Black Sea to Mediterranean, a level one player described as extortionate.
Traders said offers for Russian heating oil were around high cif Med quotes +$3.75 basis Genoa with bids around +$2.75.
High sulphur fuel prices were steady to firmer with good demand seen for quality bunker fuels.
Traders said Romanian buying for Jan had mostly been satisfied and no more buying is expected until February.
Recent tenders from Malta and Syria have soaked up supplies of quality bunker fuels but traders said there was still some good buying interest and saw prices holding firm.
High sulphur cracked cif cargoes were valued around $120 a tonne cif Med with quality bunker fuel a premium of $1-$2.

A Turkish Tender for around 50,000 tonnes for end-Jan continued to provide limited support the low sulphur prices, but traders said the tender could now be filled with product from the U.S. of Caribbean where stocks are running high.
